content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of bile acid synthesis disorders caused by single-enzyme defects (SEDs) at a dosage of 10-15 mg/kg/day, administered orally once daily or divided into two doses per day. It is also approved as an adjunctive therapy for peroxisomal disorders (PDs), including Zellweger spectrum disorders, in patients who present with liver disease, steatorrhea, or complications arising from reduced absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. The safety and efficacy of this treatment for extrahepatic manifestations of bile acid synthesis disorders due to SEDs or PDs have not been established. For patients under three weeks of age, the safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been determined. For those aged three weeks or older, the recommended dosage is 10-15 mg/kg/day, administered orally once daily or divided into two doses per day. Certain drug interactions can increase the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. These include medications such as atazanavir, atorvastatin, bosentan, clarithromycin, cyclosporine, dipyridamole, disulfiram, eluxadoline, fenofibrate, fenofibrate micronized, fenofibric acid, glimepiride, glyburide, isradipine, ketoconazole, levoketoconazole, lopinavir, loratadine, losartan, lovastatin, midazolam, mifepristone, pioglitazone, pitavastatin, ranolazine, repaglinide, rifampin, ritonavir, rosiglitazone, simvastatin, spironolactone, and tipranavir. Concomitant use of these drugs should be avoided or closely monitored, as they may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, potentially leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, serum transaminases and bilirubin levels should be monitored closely. Additionally, bile acid-binding agents such as cholestyramine, colesevelam, and colestipol can reduce the levels or effects of cholic acid by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. To minimize this interaction, cholic acid should be taken at least one hour before or four to six hours after these agents, or as far apart as possible. In summary, careful monitoring and dose adjustments are required when using cholic acid in combination with other medications that may alter its metabolism, elimination, or absorption.
